name: Thiopental
metabolism: Almost completely broken down. It is extremely fat soluble and most of the breaking down happens in the liver, but it is released slowly from the fat stores it settles into and is turned over very slowly: in one hour only 10-15% is broken down, mostly in the liver. Only about 0.3% comes out unchanged in the urine. After a single intravenous dose it spreads out over 2-4 hours and is then cleared over 9-11 hours. At a therapeutic level 80-90% is bound to blood proteins. It reaches the blood-rich parts of the brain very quickly, then spreads out to the other tissues.
summary: Thiopental, commonly given as sodium thiopental, is a rapid-onset, short-acting barbiturate general anesthetic.
